title: String to Integer (atoi)
summary: Implement the myAtoi function to convert a string into a 32-bit signed integer.
statement: Implement the myAtoi function to convert a string into a 32-bit signed integer. First, ignore any leading whitespace. Next, determine the sign by checking for a leading '-' or '+', assuming positive if neither is present. Convert the string by reading digits, skipping leading zeros, and stopping at the first non-digit character or the end of the string. If no digits are read, return 0. Round the integer to fit within the 32-bit signed integer range [-2^31, 2^31 - 1]. Return the integer as the result.
constraints: 0–200 characters consisting of English letters, digits, spaces, '+', '-', and '.'.
Skip leading spaces, consume at most one sign, then read consecutive digits until the first other character. No digits means zero.
Clamp to [-2^31, 2^31−1]. Spaces after a sign are not skipped.
target_space_complexity: O(n) bits for the bounded input accumulator
hints: Parsing has ordered phases: spaces, optional sign, digits, then stop.
Use an index and stop digit accumulation immediately on a non-digit.
Skip only initial spaces, consume one sign, repeatedly multiply the value by ten and add a digit, then apply sign and clamp.
A second sign or a space after the sign ends parsing before any digits are read.
editorial: Walk the input once. The initial-space loop must happen before sign handling, not during digit parsing. After an optional sign, accumulate only the consecutive digit run. Applying the sign to a zero accumulator naturally handles missing digits. Clamp the signed result to the 32-bit interval. A regular-expression prefix capture plus Python integer conversion provides an independent oracle.
